meta.title: OpenCinema — Your agent. Your canvas. Your film.
meta.description: A local, open-source video workbench your agent operates. Codex, Claude Code or any MCP agent does the planning; OpenCinema provides the node canvas, image and video tools, 3D previs, shot review and the final edit.

title: Your agent.
Your canvas.
Your film.
hero.lede: A local video workbench your agent operates. Codex, Claude Code or any MCP agent does the planning. OpenCinema gives it a node canvas, image and video tools, 3D previs, shot review and the final cut, and keeps you in control of every shot.
hero.shotAlt: The OpenCinema canvas: a brief, reference stills, a reference clip and an audio bed wired into a Blockout previs, an image generation node and a video generation node.

works.label: Works with the agent you already use
works.note: Plain MCP. No lock-in, no proprietary agent.

steps.title: Direct
steps.text: Select one node, a group of shots, or nothing at all. Describe the change in the composer. The scope is yours to set.
steps.alt: The composer with its scope set to one video generation node and five references.

steps.title: See
steps.text: Your agent works on the same canvas you are looking at. Open an editor, paint a selection, adjust a reference, keep a take you like.
steps.alt: The image editor with inpaint, crop, grid split, lighting, angle and panorama tools.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Review every candidate against six checks. Replace only the shot that failed. Render the full cut with its audio track.
steps.alt: A video node with its media editing tools: trim, frames, audio, frame analysis, review, speed, transcription.

features.label: Features
features.title: One canvas takes a film from idea to final cut.

rows.title: Every asset and every step is a node.
rows.text: Script, stills, clips, audio, previs, generation, review and the edit plan live on one canvas. Edges are reference relationships. Thirteen node plugins ship built in, from text and media to analysis and generation, plus a collaboration extension.
points: Everything the agent does is a visible state change
rows.alt: A connected canvas with text, media, previs and generation nodes.

rows.title: You decide what the agent may touch.
rows.text: The composer acts on your selection: one node, a marquee of nodes, or the whole canvas. Generation nodes can switch between generating and letting the agent adjust the node itself. References are numbered so you can see what the model will receive.
points: One node, N nodes, or the canvas
Manual and agent edits share one undo history
rows.alt: The composer showing the scope: Shot 02 candidates, five references.

rows.title: Change only what matters.
rows.text: Paint a selection and only that region changes. Crop and transform, split a grid, relight, change the angle, capture a panorama. Trim clips, extract audio, separate tracks, change speed and transcribe, all through local FFmpeg.
points: Image: inpaint, crop, grid split, lighting, angle, panorama
Video: trim, frames, audio, speed, frame analysis
Results become new nodes; sources stay untouched
rows.alt: The image editor open on a rainy harbor still.

rows.title: See the shot before you generate it.
rows.text: Block the action and the camera on a white-model stage. Export RGB, depth and normal layers per shot and freeze them as reference nodes for generation. Previs and depth are references for framing and rhythm, not a motion lock.
points: Characters, set pieces, camera blocking, takes
RGB, depth and normal exports per shot
Frame analysis, pose tracking and relative depth from real footage
rows.alt: The Blockout previs editor with a mannequin on a white-model stage.

rows.title: Your providers. Your keys. Your machine.
rows.text: Connect Volcengine Ark Seedance, fal, Replicate or any OpenAI-compatible video service, or import a custom provider from a JSON manifest. Credentials live in local settings; agents only ever see whether one is configured.
points: FFmpeg and the depth model prepared explicitly and pinned by hash
Go server listens on loopback only

cards.title: See the plan first
cards.text: Before anything is paid for, the generation plan shows the final prompt, the real model parameters and the role of every reference: instruction, identity, composition, motion or exclude.

cards.title: Six checks, your call
cards.text: Direction, action, identity, continuity, unexpected cuts, deformation and branding. A candidate is approved only when you mark every check and write what you saw. Rejected candidates stay in the project.

cards.title: Replace one shot, keep the rest
cards.text: The edit plan holds 2 to 16 shots, in and out points, output spec and one audio track. Swap a single shot; the others never move. Rendering creates a new cut and keeps the old one.

film.label: The film
film.title: Thirty seconds. Every frame drawn in code.
film.text: The launch film is built from the same design system as the product. No stock, no generated footage, no screenshots: every interface element is live state rendered frame by frame.

start.label: Get started
start.title: Build it, open a folder, connect your agent.
start.text: 0.4.0 is in development. Source builds need Bun 1.3.14+, Go 1.26+ and Node.js 22+. Running a packaged plugin needs Node.js 22+ only.
start.build:
git clone https://github.com/junjamrk/OpenCinema.git
cd OpenCinema
bun install --frozen-lockfile
bun run build
bun start
start.buildNote: Open http://127.0.0.1:47920 and point it at any folder.
start.agentNote: Codex: codex plugin add opencinema@openCinemaStandalone. Any MCP client can copy the connection from the settings panel.

community.label: Open source
community.title: Built in the open.
community.text: MIT licensed. A Go server, a React canvas, a framework-independent editing session and a node SDK, all in one repository. Issues, pull requests and node plugins are welcome.

cards.title: Write a node
cards.text: A node is a package that exports a plugin definition and registers Zod-typed tools. Your UI and the agent call the same implementation.

cards.title: Add a provider
cards.text: A service that speaks an existing protocol needs only a JSON manifest. Unmapped references are refused, not dropped.

cards.title: Shape the tools
cards.text: Every tool has a live schema, output validation and annotations. Errors carry a machine code and a recovery action.

honest: AI generation uses providers you configure and may cost money. No host subscription includes a video model.
Previs, white model and depth are references. Motion analysis tracks pose and 2D camera motion, not a 3D solve.
Review is a recorded decision made by a person.

market.metaTitle: OpenCinema Plugin Market — install new nodes for the canvas
market.metaDescription: Install-only catalog of OpenCinema node plugins. Every package is a static install.json verified by SHA-256 before the local server installs it.
market.title: Give the canvas new abilities.
market.lede: Node plugins add tools your agent can discover and call. The market is a static catalog: the workbench downloads a package, checks its SHA-256 against this index, shows you what it is, and only then installs it on your machine.

steps.title: Open the market
steps.text: In the workbench open Settings → Plugins → Open plugin market. The list below appears in the app.

steps.title: Download and review
steps.text: The package is downloaded and verified against the SHA-256 in this index. A review card shows id, version, size and description before anything runs.

steps.title: Install
steps.text: Confirm. The node shows up in the node menu and its tools become discoverable through getNodeTools. Agents can do the same with getPluginMarket and installMarketplacePlugin.

market.publishTitle: Ship a node of your own.
market.publishText: A node is one package: a plugin definition, Zod-typed tools, a React view and an agent.md guide. Scaffold it, build it, open a pull request that adds it to the catalog. Uploads are not supported in this MVP.
market.publishCode:
bun packages/nodeScaffold/scripts/createNode.ts myNode "My Node"
cd packages/nodes/myNode && bun run typecheck && bun run build
# then add it to site/src/marketCatalog.json and run
node site/buildMarket.mjs
market.publishNote: Read the plugin development guide for conventions: one node, one job; small verb tools; readOnly annotations; typed outputs.
honest: Installing runs plugin code on your machine with workspace access. Install only sources you trust.
The catalog is static JSON published by pull request. There is no upload, account or telemetry.
Packages are verified by size and SHA-256 against this index; a changed file is refused.
Plugins that need FFmpeg, WebGL or a provider still depend on your local setup.
